utterances.text: I will, of course, put it on the overhead projector, but it's important that I reiterate that I was never in Racak. The closest I came to it was the village of Stimlje. I wasn't there, so I cannot explain anything on the narrow area itself. I know only what I read in the reports, and I know in general where that village is located in relation to other villages and towns that I know. From this general knowledge, I have the impression that this is the Stimlje-Crnoljevo-Dulje road. If I'm right, then I can orient myself in relation to that. This is the road most probably leading to the village of Racak, but I do not know which of these settlements is Racak or whether they are all Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And what happened, on your understanding, in Racak? Describe in words or use the map as is most convenient to you. And I recognise that your sources of information come from documents but also probably from some word of mouth. Tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it's very hard for me to make use of this aerial photograph because I don't know precisely where things happened and from what direction the unit came. So it would be very difficult for me to reconstruct the event on this aerial photograph. From the information I have and the documents I looked at, this was an action to arrest a terrorist group which had its headquarters or subheadquarters here after several violent acts in which people were injured or killed. As for the time sequence, the unit, as far as I know, was attacked while it was still approaching the village. But not all parts of that unit were attacked, only certain parts of it. After approaching the village, fire was opened and this was caused by the terrorists, as we've seen in several documents, and after this a conflict ensued in a certain area or on a certain line. I do not know what the relationship was between the positions of the police unit and the positions of the terrorists because I wasn't there. In this conflict, what happened happened. And of course, after the event I know the sequence of events and all the problems connected to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I know that we are coming towards --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, we have to stop at 1.43, there being another case here this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: From what you've said is your understanding - I forecast it might have been - that this was a confrontation between a group of terrorists and the incoming Serb forces. A single group of terrorists.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The concept of "group" is not clear. Whether they were in several groups or in one large group, I don't know. I wasn't actually -- I didn't think of it in that way. But I assume that the terrorists in a place like this would have been organised into a single group or unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your understanding of where the weapons that were found by various individuals were found, where were the weapons found; with the fallen KLA fighters or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that with certainty. I do know that the police left the scene of the event and that they were unable to secure the site with the terrorists, those killed, and the weapons intact. I believe that the weapons were found later, but I don't know in what location.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And finally, because I see the time, and responsive to His Honour's invitation that I should do so, you have never seen, have you, a detailed report from the officer leading the Serb forces explaining what he did.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw only the report that is in this exhibit. This was a report from a working group tasked with establishing all the facts in relation to this event. I did not see the report drawn up by the leader of the police unit participating in the attack. I assume it is subsumed, or that the elements of that report are subsumed in the report by the working group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If I may ask one question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: One question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Such a document, a report by the leader of a police unit, might be the single most valuable document to help unravel the truth of events in Racak, mightn't it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is certainly an important document, but this working group had a broader and deeper mandate than that report itself and encompasses other information besides the information obtained from the leader of the unit who drew up that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for today and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
